If the discriminant is positive, you get two real solutions; if zero, one solution; if negative, complex numbers. Practice with simple examples to build intuition.

To find stationary points, first take the derivative f’(x) of the function. Set f’(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are critical points. Then, plug them back into f(x) to get the y-values. Finally, check if they’re maxima or minima using the second derivative test: if f''(x) > 0, it’s a minimum; if f''(x) < 0, it’s a maximum.
